protocol: choose/fit on an earlier period at sample-A stations, score on a later period, confirm on disjoint sample-B stations; 'made worse' = MAE rise > 3 % and moving-block bootstrap lower 5 % bound > 0 (FloodWatch GUIDELINES §4)

heat_index.why: the raw ECMWF heat index is about 5 °C too low against the stations' daily maximum (about 4 °C at the same hours, from an afternoon 1.9 °C too cold and a dew point 1.0 °C too low at the grid point; about 1 °C more from sampling two afternoon hours), so raw P(HI >= 42) is 0 on most days that reach 42
heat_index.formula: NWS heat index (research/heat_index.py), per member, then HI_cal = a + b * HI_raw; daily max over the member's afternoon hours
heat_index.applies_to: Open-Meteo ensemble, models=ecmwf_ifs025 (checked: its members equal the ECMWF open-data GRIB values at the nearest 0.25° point to within 0.07 °C, 2026-10-23). NOT tested for best_match or other deterministic models.

probability.method: dress each corrected member with a normal error of SD = lead_day_1.resid_sd and average P(member + error >= threshold) over members; the raw ensemble spread alone is far too narrow (its 10–90 % range held 2 % of observed maxima)
probability.status: design chosen after seeing the 2026 ENS spread; SD from 2025 only

heat_index.fitted_on: 2025-03-01..2025-10-31, 00 UTC HRES runs, 8 TMD synoptic stations (sample A)
heat_index.note: where an observed maximum for the place exists (a TMD station), 'today's observed maximum' beats the corrected model by 0.3–0.7 °C MAE at days 1–2; the app has no such observation at most points.

rain_24h.verdict: do not show a point yes/no or a point amount for heavy rain; show the ENS chance only as a coarse word (below 10 %: 'ต่ำ'; 10–40 %: 'มีโอกาส'; 40 % and more: 'โอกาสสูง'), lead with TMD's own warning, and never make 'no heavy rain' sound safe
rain_24h.why: at a station, the HRES forecast of >= 35.1 mm in 24 h has POD 0.04–0.13 and CSI 0.03–0.09 at 24–72 h in 2025 (its yes/no Brier is worse than climatology's); a lower forecast threshold chosen on 2024 (15–17.5 mm) raises POD to 0.38–0.45 and CSI to 0.08–0.12 but with FAR 0.85–0.91 and a Brier 3–5 times climatology's; the ENS probability's Brier skill against climatology is -0.08 to +0.12 (2025 and 2026), and days with P = 0 still had heavy rain 2–6 % of the time

wind_gust.why: no gust observations in the GHCNh records of the 18 stations used (2025–2026), so P(gust >= 40 km/h) was not tested; show it as unverified

pm25.method: damped ratio: forecast 24-h mean for window k = obs_mean_last_24h * (CAMS_mean(window k) / CAMS_mean(last 24 h)) ** beta_k; it is the app's planned ratio correction with the CAMS change damped (beta = 1 is the planned method, beta = 0 is persistence)
pm25.status: PROVISIONAL: the damped form was added after the first test run (post-hoc); its betas were fitted on Dec 2025–Feb 2026 only. Re-test as issued on Dec 2026–Feb 2027 (archive CAMS forecasts as issued) before calling it validated.
pm25.needs: a measured or GISTDA-estimated 24-h mean at the point; without one, show no PM2.5 outlook number (raw CAMS ran 10–13 µg/m³ low in Mar–Apr 2026 and caught 17–21 % of days >= 75.1)
pm25.planned_ratio_method_verdict: better than raw CAMS but worse than persistence at 0–24 h (made worse beyond chance at 4 of 10 stations in Mar–Apr 2026 and 7 of 10 in Oct 2026)
pm25.gbm: rejected: worse than the blend and than persistence on every disjoint test (it cannot extrapolate to burning-season levels it never saw)
pm25.caveat: CAMS history from Open-Meteo is stitched short-lead forecasts, so every CAMS-based score here is an upper bound for a 24–72 h-old forecast
pm25.fitted_on: Dec 2025–Feb 2026, Air4Thai daily means, 4 stations (sample A: 35t, 50t, 46t, 44t)

earthquake_felt.why: the IPE alone under-predicts Bangkok-metro reports in all 12 crustal events that reached them; add the Bangkok-metro term there (elsewhere the IPE is used as is: Thai-city bias 0.00 MMI)
earthquake_felt.forecasting: none: earthquakes cannot be forecast; this only estimates how strongly a quake that has happened was probably felt at a point

ipe.name: Allen, Wald & Worden (2012) active crust
ipe.source: Allen, Wald & Worden (2012) J. Seismol. 16:409-433; coefficients from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gem/oq-engine/master/openquake/hazardlib/gsim/allen_2012_ipe.py (oq-engine HEAD 91db5142ba7905a33c94483fad8f8467b5d92d6f, read 2026-10-23)

bangkok_metro_term_detail.applies_to: Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan, Pathum Thani
bangkok_metro_term_detail.status: small sample: 10 fitting events, 2 test events of one sequence

wording_mmi_thresholds.below: say 'ส่วนใหญ่ไม่รู้สึก แต่บางคนอาจรู้สึกได้ โดยเฉพาะบนอาคารสูง', never 'not felt'
wording_mmi_thresholds.never: never claim or rule out damage
wording_mmi_thresholds.predictor: AWW12 hypocentral form + the Bangkok-metro term
wording_mmi_thresholds.status: chosen on the same DYFI reports it is shown on (in-sample wording rule); DYFI over-represents people who felt the quake

flood.use: link to FloodWatch; its skill is its own (docs/research/forecast-validation-2026-10-23.md §5)
